titulo: Quiz — Four things that expire before you fly
subtitulo: The pre-flight call, and the deadlines behind it
introPt: A traveller closes the gaps in a booking a week before departure.
cenario: A phone call to the hotel, from the kitchen table.

dialogo.es: 予約の確認をお願いしたいのですが。
dialogo.pt: Hello, I'd like to confirm my booking.
dialogo.tts: 予約の確認をお願いしたいのですが。

dialogo.es: 中央区銀座一丁目二番三号です。
dialogo.tts: 中央区銀座一丁目二番三号です。

dialogo.es: メールで送ってもらえますか？
dialogo.pt: Can you send it to me by email?
dialogo.tts: メールで送ってもらえますか？

dialogo.es: はい、メールでお送りします。
dialogo.pt: Of course, I'll send it to you by email.
dialogo.tts: はい、メールでお送りします。

perguntas.pergunta: What does a European health card (GHIC or EHIC) buy you in Japan?
opcoes: Full cover, the same as travel insurance
Nothing — Japan has no reciprocal scheme, so you pay the full cost, usually up front
A free private clinic
The flight home if you are unwell
perguntas.explica: There is no GHIC/EHIC equivalent in Japan. Travel insurance with medical cover is the one document that is not optional.

perguntas.pergunta: You planned to grab a plain Suica at a machine on arrival. What now?
opcoes: They are always available at any station
A chip shortage suspended plain Suica/Pasmo sales since 2023 — buy a Welcome Suica at the airport, or Suica on your phone
Paper tickets are the only option
You must order one from home months ahead
perguntas.explica: The Welcome Suica is valid 28 days with no deposit; once loaded, an IC card works nationwide on most trains, buses and konbini.

perguntas.pergunta: Why ask for the exact address in Japanese before flying?
opcoes: It is politer than asking on arrival
A hotel name is not routable — a driver or an offline map needs the ward, district and block
Hotels charge less if you confirm
It is required by the booking site
perguntas.explica: The name is a brand. Japanese addresses go by block, and drivers usually key the hotel's phone number into the nav, so get both in writing.

perguntas.pergunta: What is «meeru de okutte moraemasu ka» / asking for it in writing for?
opcoes: Asking for the bill
Asking someone to speak more slowly
Getting the address in writing so it survives your memory and a dead phone
Asking for a different room
perguntas.explica: An address said down a phone line does not survive the walk to the taxi rank. Written down, offline, it does.

perguntas.pergunta: Cash in Japan — what is the real constraint for a visitor?
opcoes: A legal cap on how much cash you may carry
Nothing — every ATM takes foreign cards
Not a legal cap but where you can withdraw — 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) and Japan Post are the reliable ones
Cards are refused everywhere
perguntas.explica: Japan runs heavily on cash and many bank ATMs reject foreign cards or close at night. Decide the amount at home rather than assuming any machine will serve you.
